units.function: Active environment-diagnostic tests for the local Pi adapter, checking model discovery, a minimal execution probe, structured pass codes and targeted diagnosis of a stale npm package configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: The test calls the Pi adapter's testEnvironment with Company/adapter configuration. A controllable PATH resolves an executable fixture; raw environment credentials and model/cwd configuration cross into external child processes whose output is classified into health checks.
units.keyDataModels: Pi adapter environment request; command/cwd/model/env; PATH and OPENAI_API_KEY; model-list text; session/agent_start/turn_start/turn_end JSON; usage/cost; structured health code/level/hint and aggregate status.
units.lifecycle: Resolve configured binary; run model discovery; run a hello Agent turn; recognize a terminal assistant result and report passing readiness; alternatively map an npm package-registry failure to a targeted warning/remediation hint.
units.testAssessment: Both focused tests pass. The two-stage discovery-plus-execution probe gives stronger readiness evidence than checking binary existence alone, and stable check codes improve operator handling. Coverage omits executable/package identity and version, unsafe PATH resolution, cwd validation, secret references/redaction, selected-model mismatch, protocol/capability compatibility, timeout/cancel/output bounds, network policy, probe side effects, malformed streams and cleanup through finally. The stale-package decision is coupled to English npm stderr.
units.designRationale: Detect whether Pi can both enumerate the configured model surface and complete a real minimal turn, while giving an actionable warning for a known obsolete package-install path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs trustworthy Connector readiness for managed and customer-local nodes without exposing secrets or allowing a control-plane health check to become uncontrolled code/model/network execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the layered health model: passive manifest/signature/version validation, capability/model discovery and an explicitly authorized active canary. Execute probes only on the bound execution node with package identity verification, fixed executable resolution, scoped network/data policy, time/output/cost budgets and full audit. Resolve opaque secret references locally into a minimal allowlisted environment and redact all outputs. Return stable health reason codes and structured provider parameters; keep text signatures as quarantined compatibility fallbacks. Health never grants work authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: The hello probe performs an Agent/model action using credentials but is not bound to an accountable human, approved purpose, data/egress grant, budget or evidence record. A technically passing probe must remain separate from organizational authorization to execute real work.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: readiness includes both discovery and real minimal execution; results use stable codes; known install drift gets a targeted diagnostic. CRITICAL active-probe boundary: health invokes an Agent/model process and therefore consumes code, credentials, network and possibly money. HIGH secret risk: a raw API key is present in adapter environment configuration and no reference resolution/redaction is proved. HIGH executable risk: PATH is caller-controlled and no package/signature/version identity is tested. HIGH egress/cost gap: no model-call network allowlist, data policy, timeout or cost ceiling is covered. MEDIUM parser fragility: stale-package recognition depends on English npm registry text. MEDIUM lifecycle gap: cleanup is not guarded by finally and hung/malformed probes are untested.
